narrative:
The model estimates you have a 12% chance of failing your final year. While this is a relatively low probability, the system flags it as high enough that you are required to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might not pass is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. The most influential factor is your weekly study time, which is only 5-10 hours. This is lower than what most students who successfully pass tend to commit, and it pulls the prediction toward failure. Next, your record shows zero past class failures, which is actually identical to the average among students who passed and therefore helps push the outcome in a more positive direction. The third important element is your reason for choosing this school—wanting to be close to home. This choice is less common among students who go on to pass and contributes some additional influence toward the failing prediction.

Taken together, the limited study hours and your school-choice motivation outweigh the positive signal from your clean failure record, leading the model to err on the side of caution.

To improve, you should strongly consider increasing your weekly study time beyond 5-10 hours, as this appears to be the single biggest lever available to you right now. Even modest extra focused work each week could meaningfully raise your chances of passing without needing the remedial requirement.
